title: Bisect with Scripts
description: Write robust bisect scripts for complex regressions, multi-step checks, and partial test suites.

data.text: For complex regressions, a simple yes/no test is not enough. Bisect scripts can run multi-step checks, inspect logs, check for multiple symptoms, and handle edge cases. A well-written bisect script turns a manual hours-long hunt into a one-liner.
A bisect script is any program or script that exits with the appropriate code. It runs at each bisect step, in the checked-out commit's working directory. All paths are relative to that commit.

data.title: Multi-step bisect script for API regression
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# bisect-api-regression.sh

set -e

echo "Checking API response at commit $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)..."

# Step 1: Build the project
npm run build > /dev/null 2>&1
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Skipping: build fails at this commit"
  exit 125
fi

# Step 2: Start the server in background
node dist/server.js &
SERVER_PID=$?
sleep 2

# Step 3: Make the API call and check response
RESPONSE=$(curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/users/me)
if echo "$RESPONSE" | grep -q "token_expired"; then
  echo "BUG FOUND: token_expired in response"
  exit 1
else
  echo "OK: no regression"
  exit 0
fi

data.text: When a regression has multiple symptoms, your script can check for all of them and return bad if any symptom is present. This makes the script robust against false negatives.

data.title: Multi-symptom bisect script
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# bisect-regression.sh

BUG_PRESENT=0

# Check for error message in source
if grep -r "NullReferenceException" src/ 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Symptom: NullReferenceException found in source"
  BUG_PRESENT=1
fi

# Check for failing test
if npm test -- --grep "Regression test" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "failing"; then
  echo "Symptom: regression test failing"
  BUG_PRESENT=1
fi

if [ $BUG_PRESENT -eq 1 ]; then
  exit 1  # bad
else
  exit 0  # good
fi

data.text: Some commits may not build for reasons unrelated to the regression (missing dependencies, migration issues, etc.). Use exit 125 to skip them and continue the search.

data.title: Bisect script with build skip logic
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# bisect-with-skip.sh

# Install dependencies
npm install --silent > /dev/null 2>&1

# Try to build
npm run build > /dev/null 2>&1
BUILD_EXIT=$?

if [ $BUILD_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Skipping: build fails at this commit"
  exit 125
fi

# Run the specific regression test
npm test -- --grep "Bug reproduction test" 2>/dev/null
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "PASS"
  exit 0  # good
else
  echo "FAIL"
  exit 1  # bad
fi

data.title: Test reproducibility is essential
data.text: Bisect only works if your reproduction test is reliable. If the test gives different results on the same commit, bisect will give wrong results. Make your test deterministic.
For long-running bisects, log each step's result to a file. This creates an audit trail and helps diagnose bisect failures.

data.title: Bisect script with logging
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# bisect-with-logging.sh

LOG_FILE="bisect-results.log"
COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

echo "--- Testing $COMMIT ---" >> "$LOG_FILE"

# Run test
npm test -- --grep "Regression" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1
TEST_EXIT=$?

echo "Exit code: $TEST_EXIT" >> "$LOG_FILE"

if [ $TEST_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "GOOD" >> "$LOG_FILE"
  exit 0
elif [ $TEST_EXIT -eq 125 ]; then
  echo "SKIP" >> "$LOG_FILE"
  exit 125
else
  echo "BAD" >> "$LOG_FILE"
  exit 1
fi

items.question: Can my bisect script make network requests?
items.answer: Yes, but be aware that the checked-out commit may not have the server code. Build and start the server in the script if needed.

items.question: What if my test takes too long?
items.answer: Bisect is only practical if each step takes under a minute. For slow tests, use a targeted reproduction test that checks for the specific symptom.

items.question: Can I use bisect on a specific file?
items.answer: Yes. git bisect start <bad> <good> -- path/to/file limits the bisect to commits that modified that file.

items.question: How do I share a bisect script with my team?
items.answer: Commit the script to the repository (e.g., scripts/bisect-regression.sh) so teammates can reproduce your bisect steps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Bisect scripts run at each step and must exit 0, 1, or 125
Multi-step scripts can build, start servers, and run integration checks
Use exit 125 to skip commits that cannot be tested
Make tests deterministic — bisect relies on consistent results
Limit bisect to specific files with git bisect start -- <path>
